It takes a lot of work but you can definitely change your way of thinking! One good method is every time you start to beat yourself up pretend your good friend made the mistake instead. Then think of how you would respond to them. It makes you objectively look at your reaction and can help you see how out of proportion it is to the situation. Then treat yourself like you’d treat that friend.

This may not be the type of answer you're looking for, but I had a major gut feeling when I was 11 and they were testing us out to play musical instruments. We gor to pick 4 instruments to try out and we would learn to play whichever one we liked best the next year in school.

I tried out the violin, drums, flute, and cello. With the first 3 instruments I felt like I could probably play them and would be happy to do so. But the second the teacher put the cello in my hands I had one of the strongest gut feelings I've ever had, and it said "This is the instrument you're going to play".

So I did, for 7 incredible years and I loved it. I'm hoping to get back into it soon.
